name: Discover Rolf's Fate
summary: Guard Thomas waits for news of Rolf and Malakai, missing near Stone Cairn Lake. Malakai's half-eaten remains and webbed tracks point toward a murloc village.

sections.title: A Trail of Webbed Tracks
sections.body: Malakai's half-eaten remains lie by the shore. Webbed footprints mark the mud and lead east along the water's edge. They run straight to a ramshackle murloc camp.

sections.title: The End of Patrol
sections.body: You follow the tracks into the heart of the coastal murloc settlement. Another corpse lies there, stripped by the creatures. An inscribed medallion around the dead soldier's neck names him Footman Rolf Hartford. Neither guard survived the ambush.

faq.answer: Rolf Hartford was a Stormwind footman assigned to patrol eastern Elwynn Forest under Guard Thomas, alongside Guard Malakai. Murlocs overwhelmed and killed both guards near Stone Cairn Lake.
Rolf's corpse lies farther east along the southern shore of Stone Cairn Lake, inside a murloc village near the lake's border.

faq.q: Why were the guards out near Stone Cairn Lake?
faq.answer: Guard Thomas stationed guards along eastern Elwynn's rivers and lakes to watch for murloc and gnoll incursions. The patrols were understaffed and vulnerable to sudden, coordinated attacks.

faq.q: How do you confirm the corpse belongs to Rolf?
faq.answer: A metal medallion hangs around the torn corpse's neck. The inscription names him Footman Rolf Hartford.
With the fates of Malakai and Rolf confirmed, you are tasked with returning west to the bridge at Eastvale Logging Camp. There, you report the grim news to Guard Thomas.

faq.q: Are the murlocs in Stone Cairn Lake an unusual threat?
faq.answer: Murlocs in Elwynn have grown unusually aggressive and coordinated. They are pushing inland into Stone Cairn Lake and the rivers, threatening local trade and lone patrols alike.

angles.text: Finding Rolf shows how exposed Stormwind's rural borders are. Garrison shortages leave even basic patrols open to deadly attacks from the wild.
As a warrior, you see in Rolf Hartford's body the bloody reality faced by footmen serving the realm.
